working_title: Why a 10-minute walk after meals matters

sources.title: The Acute Effects of Interrupting Prolonged Sitting Time in Adults with Standing and Light-Intensity Walking on Biomarkers of Cardiometabolic Health

scenes.narration: Right after you eat, your blood sugar starts climbing. Here's the easiest way to flatten it.
Researchers pooled seven studies comparing sitting, standing, and light walking after meals.
Even two to five minutes of light walking lowered the blood sugar spike compared with sitting.
The best window? Within about an hour of eating, while glucose is rising.
So next time you finish a meal, don't sink into the couch. Take a short walk. Your body will thank you.
